items.title: EU nations unveil Rwanda deal for migrant return hub
items.standfirst: Five EU countries including Germany and Denmark on Monday unveiled a deal to establish a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda -- the first such facility outside the bloc. The group, also comprising Austria, Greece and the Netherlands, has been gunning to open a "return-hub" despite rights groups' concerns, after the European Union cleared the way with a recent toughening of migration rules. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.

items.title: UEFA backs France's Diallo to stand against Infantino in FIFA election
items.standfirst: European football's governing body UEFA has given its "unanimous" backing to French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino in March's FIFA presidential election, it said in a statement Monday. Under its Slovenian president Aleksander Ceferin, UEFA has led the opposition to Infantino since his announcement in late July of a project to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes speaks with Dr. Emanuel Macedo de Medeiros, Co-founder and Global CEO of the Sport Integrity Global Alliance.

items.title: French film star Depardieu drops appeal against sexual conviction
items.standfirst: French film star Gérard Depardieu on Monday dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women during the filming of a movie in 2021 and issued "sincere apologies" for his past behaviour on set. "For a long time on film sets, I hid behind provocation and ribald humour," Depardieu, 77, said in the statement, withdrawing his appeal on the day it was set to go to trial. "I believed my remarks and some of my gestures would be without consequences" for those involved, he said. "They were not, particularly coming from a powerful figure such as I once was."
